raw.assessment: The incumbent appears adequate for some stable courses: unchanged-assignment centers had a seven-minute median, versus 17 minutes overall. Intended course coverage was 32/40, below the 95% target. Assignment changes accompany six of eight affected exports, making current-assignment semantics a plausible contributor, not an established cause. The two renamed-course cases limit any assignment-only explanation. Execution takes under 75 seconds, while replacements arrive much later; faster execution alone has little evidential support. No sampled cross-center rows were found, but the split-course center was absent, so isolation there remains untested. Spreadsheet handling and timetable accuracy remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a historical week may exclude otherwise intended course attendance; resolving membership against the requested week's assignment history could prevent those omissions.
openings.delta: Makes the assignment-change association testable through a specific export-selection mechanism.
openings.prediction: In otherwise identical fabricated cases, changing only the current assignment changes historical export membership; week-effective selection restores the independently specified membership. Rename-only failures may persist.
openings.probe: Replay fabricated midweek reassignment cases in staging, including a course with attendance before and after transfer. Compare emitted course and participant membership with a coordinator-agreed weekly expectation. Exercise simultaneous attendance entry and tenant isolation while retaining the documented CSV. Check history availability and estimate effort before selecting an implementation within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Reliable effective dates exist or can be recovered within budget.
Requested-week membership can be specified independently of current assignment.

openings.claim: Do renamed courses trigger replacement requests because records are missing, or because correct records cannot be matched to coordinators' timetable labels?
openings.delta: Separates export omission from recognition or timetable disagreement, which require different remedies.
openings.prediction: Recognition failures retain the expected fabricated attendance records despite reported absence; actual omissions lack them before spreadsheet import.
openings.probe: During the two short sessions, have consenting coordinators specify expectations for fabricated renamed-course examples, then download, check and import unchanged-schema CSVs. Observe where disagreement first appears and time each step. Compare expected and emitted records inside staging and authorized workspaces.
assumptions: Fabricated rename examples approximate relevant handling behavior.
Small-session findings require confirmation across the next 40 exports.

raw.assessment: Outcome payment could favor selection correctness or faster recovery. Assignment changes and renaming correlate with affected exports; causation and implementation feasibility remain unproven. The sample does not establish isolation for split courses.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a fixed fee with a holdback tied to the stated outcome across a predeclared 40-export cohort would favor a center/week course manifest independent of displayed names and current instructor assignment.
openings.delta: Reward preventing rework. Gaming could exclude difficult exports, redefine intended sets, or transfer checking to coordinators; retain every cohort export and count checking time.
openings.prediction: If selection semantics explain the association, a reconciled weekly manifest reduces reassignment and rename omissions without increasing handling time.
openings.probe: In first coordinator sessions, reconcile fabricated intended sets before revealing outputs. Compare incumbent and manifest selection on reassignment, rename, and split cases; check unauthorized-center exclusion, unchanged CSV imports, and concurrent attendance entry.
assumptions: Stable course identity and week-specific evidence exist or can be captured within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
Participant names remain private and authorized; selection reads do not block attendance entry.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: holding back payment until a correction produces a usable file would favor authorized private self-service correction and regeneration using the documented CSV schema.
openings.delta: Reward restoring usability. Gaming could close requests after fast but unchanged exports; require intended-set and import checks and count all correction time.
openings.prediction: If request handling dominates recovery, corrected files arrive sooner; active handling may remain unchanged if checking and importing dominate.
openings.probe: In second sessions, compare provider-mediated and self-service recovery on fabricated incorrect exports. Separately time active work and elapsed recovery; verify sets, imports, isolation, and simultaneous attendance entry. Repeated identical omissions reject regeneration alone as sufficient.
assumptions: A bounded correction interface and export execution fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.
Corrections can be restricted to authorized center/week selection without stopping attendance entry.

openings.claim: Week-effective instructor membership may prevent omissions.
openings.discriminator: Changing only current assignment alters historical membership.
openings.probe: Replay fabricated transfers, including attendance before/after; compare independently agreed expectations.
openings.uncertainty: Selection dependency, reliable history and affordable recovery unproven; rename failures may persist.

openings.claim: Rename complaints may reflect omission, recognition or timetable disagreement.
openings.discriminator: Expected records absent before import versus present but unrecognized.
openings.probe: Observe fabricated rename downloads, checking and imports; time each step and locate first disagreement.
openings.uncertainty: Timetable accuracy/update timing and example representativeness unknown.

openings.claim: Fixed-fee outcome holdback may favor independent center/week manifests.
openings.discriminator: Manifest selection reduces reassignment/rename omissions without extra handling.
openings.probe: Agree fabricated expectations before revealing incumbent/manifest outputs; compare reassignment, rename and split cases.
openings.uncertainty: Stable identities/week evidence and feasibility unknown; cohort exclusion, redefined expectations or shifted checking could game payment.

openings.claim: Usable-correction payment holdback may favor authorized private self-service correction/regeneration.
openings.discriminator: Elapsed recovery improves; active handling may not.
openings.probe: Compare mediated/self-service recovery; time active/elapsed work; verify sets/imports. Repeated omissions defeat regeneration alone.
openings.uncertainty: Interface feasibility and request-handling dominance unknown; unchanged fast files could game payment.

post_distill.decision: Probe before implementation. All paths require private authorized names, documented CSV, uninterrupted attendance entry, six engineer-days and existing hosting. Test isolation including splits; sampled safety is incomplete. Use six coordinators/two sessions; predeclare all 40 exports, count all checking/correction time, retain original success thresholds. Synthetic associations establish no causation.
